title: Privacy & operational fit eval - Catalyst Lenders

Team agreed to baseline POC for Dedicated with ability to evaluate Private on air-gapped requirements; Redwood to send compliance artifacts and sample retention configs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood Solutions), Aisha Khan (Catalyst Head of Security), Tom Reeves (Platform Lead), Jenny Li (Compliance), Ravi Patel (DevOps)

Summary: Quick discovery on residency and logging. Customer leaning Dedicated but has strict key residency and some on-prem audit needs. Redwood to propose POC and send compliance pack.

[00:00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intros, then we wanted to understand the residency and ops constraints you mentioned in the intake form.
[00:00:22] Aisha (Catalyst): Thanks Lena. I'll level set — Catalyst is a mid-market lender, highly regulated, we store loan docs with PII, some health-related disclosure in certain products so HIPAA overlap, and absolutely need control over keys and logs.
[00:00:38] Tom: We're mainly interested in a path that avoids cross-border movement of EU data, and some states mandate retention windows.
[00:00:47] Marco (Redwood SE): Got it. Quick question — when you say "keys and logs" are you requiring the keys to remain in your KMS in-country, or just that access is auditable?
[00:00:57] Aisha: Prefer keys resident in our KMS — we use a cloud KMS with a regional key ring in eu-west-1 for EU customers. For the US... we have more latitude but still need strict access controls and audit trails.
[00:01:12] Jenny (Compliance): Also, log retention: security wants 7 years for certain event types, but product teams only want 90 days for request metadata. We need redaction for raw transcripts — specifically PII removed before logs leave the processing boundary.
[00:01:30] Lena: Okay, that's helpful. Our product supports three deployment modes — Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with tenancy isolation), and Private (VPC/on-prem package). For key residency, Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS via external key wrap — we can ensure keys never leave your control. Private gives the tightest guarantee because you run the control plane on-prem.
[00:01:56] Ravi (DevOps): To be clear, for Dedicated, are there networking egress paths back to Redwood control plane or logs? We have strict egress policies.
[00:02:06] Marco: For Dedicated we offer a private peering option; control plane calls can be routed through your VPC and we support region-locking so routing stays in-region. There are still optional telemetry channels for observability but they can be toggled off and logs delivered to your S3/KV store.
[00:02:24] Tom: What about audit logs — can we get an immutable stream to our audit collector? We need tamper evidence.
[00:02:31] Marco: Yes, we can stream WORM-style logs or push to your SIEM; we also sign logs and include sequencing for tamper detection. Implementation varies by deployment.
[00:02:43] Aisha: HIPAA — are you a BAA signatory for Hosted or Dedicated?
[00:02:48] Lena: We can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private; Hosted requires a review but we have customers on Hosted under BAAs in specific arrangements — we'll surface exact language in the artifacts.
[00:02:58] Jenny: And what about data minimization — can we redact PHI before it's written to any logs?
[00:03:04] Marco: We have configurable redaction pipelines: model output redaction, prefix KV caching redaction, and log sanitization rules. Some fields can be redacted at the runtime layer before being persisted; others require a post-processing step which we can run in your VPC for Private deployments.
[00:03:20] [crosstalk] Ravi: So if we choose Dedicated, would the redaction run inside our network?
[00:03:24] Marco: With Dedicated plus private peering you can route logs to your log collector and run redaction in your environment; for absolute guarantees you pick Private.
[00:03:31] Lena: Real quick, could you outline the success criteria for a POC? What do you need to see?
[00:03:36] Jenny: We need proof that no EU customer data leaves EU regions, that keys are controlled by us, and that logs can be redacted and retained per our windows. Also, latency SLAs for loan decision flows — sub 250ms 95th for short prompts.
[00:03:50] Tom: And show cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated at our expected qps.
[00:03:55] Marco: Great — we can run a POC with a small Dedicated pool, route traffic from eu-west and us-east regions, run our benchmark harness, and demonstrate redaction and streaming to your SIEM.
[00:04:08] Aisha: That sounds reasonable. A few other checks: do you provide evidence for encryption in transit and at rest with KMS keys in our control?
[00:04:17] Lena: Yes, we use TLS 1.2+ in transit, and for at-rest we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM integrations for Private deployments. We'll include the KMS integration guide in the compliance pack.
[00:04:29] [00:10:00] Marco: Diving into specifics — for Dedicated, we recommend quantization-friendly model variants to reduce GPU footprint; that affects cost but not audit controls. Any constraints on model variants from a compliance standpoint?
[00:10:14] Tom: No, product team is fine as long as outputs are audited and we can reproduce prompts.
[00:10:22] Jenny: One red flag — retention of raw prompt/response pairs. We can't keep raw transcripts for more than 90 days for consumer-facing flows; internal audit events may go longer. Can Redwood partition logs by log-type?
[00:10:34] Marco: Yes — we allow per-route retention and redaction rules; you can create a route for production that strips prompts and only logs metadata, while a test route keeps full traces for debugging.
[00:10:45] Aisha: About geofencing, how strict is region locking? If a failover happens, could requests route to another region?
[00:10:53] Lena: We have policy-based routing. You can specify strict region lock — in that mode automated failover will not cross regions; you can choose to allow cross-region fallback for availability.
[00:11:04] Ravi: For regulatory audits, we need a chain of custody for keys and for who accessed which model instance. Does Redwood provide user-level access logs?
[00:11:13] Marco: We emit granular audit logs — API keys, team members, actions like deploy/rollback — and integrate with your SSO (SAML/SCIM) so identities map to your directory.
[00:11:24] [00:20:00] Jenny: There's also the question of data at rest in caches — KV cache could contain PII. How do we ensure cache eviction or encryption per-tenant?
[00:20:09] Marco: KV cache is ephemeral by default but for Dedicated we can configure TTLs and encryption with customer keys; for Private you have full control. We also support automatic prefix caching with optional encryption.
[00:20:24] Tom: Okay, licensing and contract questions — what's included in Dedicated pricing? Is there a monthly commitment and overage model?
[00:20:31] Lena: Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commitment and defined throughput; there are burst policies you can enable. We'll attach pricing tiers but we can also model your expected qps to show delta vs Hosted.
[00:20:41] Aisha: Legal will want to see subprocessor list and dataflow diagrams. Can you provide a list and an example architecture?
[00:20:48] Priya (Redwood Solutions): Yes, we'll include subprocessors and a control-plane/data-plane diagram showing optional dataflows and routing. We'll highlight what stays in-region under each deployment.
[00:20:58] [00:30:00] Marco: A quick note on redaction approaches — we have deterministic rule-based redaction and ML-assisted PHI scrubbing. For high-assurance flows we recommend running scrubbing inside your VPC or on Private. The ML scrubber has precision recall metrics which we will include.
[00:30:18] Aisha: Can you give an example of the scrubber's false positive rate? We can't have critical loan data removed incorrectly.
[00:30:24] Marco: We'll share metrics; the scrubber is tunable and you can specify whitelists for structured fields. For POC we can run sample payloads to measure FP/FN.
[00:30:36] Tom: On the SSO side, we use Okta. How long does SCIM provisioning and role sync take?
[00:30:43] Priya: Usually a few hours to configure and test; we support SAML for login and SCIM for provisioning. Role mapping is customizable.
[00:30:51] Jenny: Any controls for redaction previews so compliance can validate before data is deleted?
[00:30:57] Marco: We can provide a pre-processing buffer — a preview queue that compliance can review in a secure workspace before final persistence. That would typically be part of the POC.
[00:31:08] [00:40:00] Aisha: What about evidence for HIPAA controls — do you provide encryption algorithms and HSM attestation?
[00:40:08] Lena: We'll include algorithm lists (AES-GCM, RSA wrap), and for HSM we can provide attestations and integration notes; for Private deployments you can use your HSM.
[00:40:18] Ravi: If we need an air-gapped option for certain customers, is Private fully air-gappable?
[00:40:24] Marco: Private can be deployed on-prem with no external egress; some control-plane features require periodic connectivity for updates but there is an air-gapped mode where those are handled via signed bundles. We'll outline the operational tradeoffs.
[00:40:37] Aisha: Great. Last bit — incident response. We need commitments on notification windows and logs in case of suspected exfiltration.
[00:40:46] Lena: We have incident SLAs for Dedicated/Private; we'll include standard notification windows and an example runbook. For Hosted customers, incident handling depends on contract tier.
[00:40:58] Tom: Perfect. Anything else on your end?
[00:41:03] Priya: We'll include a sample benchmark run with your traffic profile and show latency percentiles and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:41:11] Jenny: And we want to review the BAA and subprocessors.
[00:41:15] Lena: Noted. To recap next steps — Lena will send compliance pack (SOC2, HIPAA, subprocessors), Marco will send POC plan and benchmark harness, customer will confirm legal/security reviewers and provide required log types and retention windows.
[00:41:33] Aisha: Thanks, that works. Can we aim to have artifacts by next week?
[00:41:37] Lena: We'll target Feb 2 for the pack and Feb 4 for the POC plan.
[00:41:43] [00:50:00] Closing chatter and scheduling follow-up.
